Guided onboarding: generate config, sign up, connect project

## Usage

`circleci onboard [path] [flags]`

## Arguments

`<path>` is the directory to onboard. Defaults to the current directory.

## Flags

| Flag               | Description                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--no-browser`     | Print the signup URL instead of opening a browser                  |
| `--org string`     | Organization slug (e.g. gh/myorg) or UUID to set the project up in |
| `--repo-id string` | Repository ID, if it cannot be resolved from the git remote        |
| `--scan`           | Skip prompt: set up this repo on CircleCI                          |
| `--signup`         | Skip prompt: sign up for CircleCI                                  |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Interactive mode: choose repo setup or signup: 
  `circleci onboard`
- Set up the current directory (skip the choice prompt): 
  `circleci onboard --scan`
- Set up in a named org (required when you belong to several): 
  `circleci onboard --scan --org gh/acme`
- Sign up for CircleCI (no repo needed): 
  `circleci onboard --signup`

## Details

Prompts for repo setup or signup unless --scan or --signup is given. Writes a
starter config if none exists, creates and follows the project, adds a trigger.
--org is required when you belong to several orgs and cannot be prompted.
